title: EAMET: ROBUST MASSIVE MODEL EDITING VIA EMBEDDING ALIGNMENT OPTIMIZATION
claim: Existing methods fail to keep memory and key embeddings aligned, breaking effectiveness and robustness; ours aligns them and passes every check.
layout: 2 regions: embedding diagrams left, checklist table right with ✗/✓ columns
description: A top line shows an example edit, 'Jeep Commander is created by Jeep → Honda', with a scissors EDIT arrow. Below, the left side has two stacked diagrams of paired rows of colored cells labeled memory and key. The upper one, 'Current Methods', has red outlines and mismatched shading, with a large red X over it. The lower one, 'EAMET (ours)', has blue outlines and a blue arrow between the rows showing alignment. A dashed vertical line separates this from a right-hand table. The table has two columns, 'Current Methods' and 'EAMET'. Its rows are grouped under Effectiveness (two probability inequality and argmax formulas) and Robustness ([PREFIX] Sentence, and multiple sentences sharing the subject Jeep Commander). Current Methods gets a mix of green checks and red crosses. EAMET gets green checks on every row. The eye goes first to the red X and the column of marks.
caption: Illustration of current methods and our proposed EAMET in evaluating massive editing. Here, "[PREFIX] Sentence" and "\{Sentence $\mid$ $s_i=Jeep Commander$\}" denote the scenarios where the edited knowledge is preceded by prefixes and where multiple facts share the same subject, respectively.
abstract: Model editing techniques are essential for efficiently updating knowledge in large language models (LLMs). However, the effectiveness of existing approaches degrades in massive editing scenarios, particularly when evaluated with practical metrics. Their robustness is also limited in context-rich settings or when editing multiple facts of the same subject simultaneously. We attribute these failures to the embedding misalignment among knowledge items, which undermines editing reliability at scale. To address this, we propose EAMET (Embedding Alignment Model Editing in Transformers), which addresses this issue by aligning the space of key and residual embeddings. Extensive experiments across six LLMs and three datasets demonstrate that EAMET consistently outperforms existing methods, achieving about 90\% editing efficacy when editing 10k facts. Codes and datasets are publicly available at https://ybdai7.github.io/eamet-page/.
